question: The image is a single axial slice from a brain MRI examination of a patient with glioblastoma (skull-stripped and registered to a standard template). Which MRI sequence does this image show?

The image is an axial slice of a post-contrast T1-weighted brain MRI in radiological convention (the patient's right side is on the left of the image; anterior is at the top). Where is the main tumor region (enhancing tumor, necrosis or resection cavity, not the surrounding edema) on this slice? Divide the brain on this slice into right and left hemispheres at the midline and into anterior and posterior halves at the midpoint of its front-to-back extent.

facts_used.key_rule: largest tumour-core component on the displayed slice

question: Three post-contrast T1-weighted axial slices of the same patient are shown, each at the largest cross-section of the same enhancing lesion (the enhancing lesion nearest the largest enhancing region on the post-operative baseline scan, followed across scans), in time order: the post-operative baseline scan (image 1), the earlier scan with the smallest enhancing lesion (the nadir, image 2) and the follow-up scan (image 3). Pixels are 1 mm in the original scan, and a 20 mm scale bar is drawn on each image. Apply the RANO enhancement criteria to the enhancing lesion. Measurable means at least 10 mm by 10 mm. Progression is a 25% or greater increase in the product of the two largest perpendicular diameters relative to the nadir, or a new measurable enhancing lesion. Response is judged against the post-operative baseline: partial response is a 50% or greater decrease, complete response is no remaining measurable enhancing disease, otherwise stable disease. T2/FLAIR changes, steroid dose and clinical status are not provided. What is the response category at follow-up?
image_labels: scan with the smallest enhancing lesion so far (nadir)

facts_used.key_rule: image-derived RANO-style enhancement category (bidimensional products on the displayed slices); the expert rating is recorded, not the key

question: A 59-year-old female with glioblastoma (MGMT promoter methylated; IDH wild type) had a complete resection of the enhancing tumor and then standard chemoradiotherapy (radiotherapy with concurrent temozolomide), followed by adjuvant temozolomide. No second surgery or second-line treatment has been given. The follow-up MRI is 27 weeks after surgery and the patient is alive at this time. Using only the information above and your earlier assessment of this patient, estimate the probability that the patient will die within 52 weeks after this scan.

facts_used.time_origin_assumption: survival time and scan weeks share the surgery-week origin

question: A 59-year-old female with glioblastoma (MGMT promoter methylated; IDH wild type) had a complete resection of the enhancing tumor and then standard chemoradiotherapy (radiotherapy with concurrent temozolomide), followed by adjuvant temozolomide. No second surgery or second-line treatment has been given. This MRI is 27 weeks after surgery; chemoradiotherapy ended about 17 weeks before this scan. Using your earlier assessment of this patient, what is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Continue adjuvant temozolomide unchanged and plan the next surveillance MRI in 8 to 12 weeks.
options.B: Continue adjuvant temozolomide for now and repeat the MRI in 4 to 8 weeks before changing therapy.
options.C: Change therapy now: bring re-resection, second-line treatment or a clinical trial to tumor board.
options.D: Stop tumor-directed treatment and move to best supportive care with no further imaging plan.

correct_answer_text: Continue adjuvant temozolomide unchanged and plan the next surveillance MRI in 8 to 12 weeks.

tcm_rule.rule: non-PD -> continue; PD and <= 12 weeks after radiotherapy -> repeat MRI first; PD and later -> change therapy (RANO 2010; Stupp schedule assumed)
